items.followUp: Describe the use of enzymes in the food and detergent industries.

rubric.why: Credits a correct use of enzymes in detergents.
rubric.description: Enzymes in detergents break down stains and improve cleaning.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct detergent application.

rubric.why: Credits examples of enzyme use in food processing.
rubric.description: Enzymes are used in food processing, including cheese-making, baking and fruit-juice processing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for at least one valid food-industry use.

rubric.description: Enzymes help process or finish fabrics in the textile industry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid textile application.

rubric.description: Enzymes are used to remove hair from hides or soften leather.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid leather application.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are used in detergents to break down stains and improve cleaning.
In the food industry, enzymes are used in cheese-making, baking and fruit-juice processing.
In the textile industry, enzymes help process and finish fabrics.
In the leather industry, enzymes help remove hair from hides or soften leather.

items.followUp: Define molecular biology and state how it differs from cell biology.

rubric.why: Credits identifying cell biology as a branch of biology.
rubric.description: Cell biology is a branch of biology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the field as a branch of biology.

rubric.why: Credits stating what cell biology studies.
rubric.description: It studies cells, including their structure and functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the field studies cells.

modelAnswer: Cell biology is the branch of biology that studies cells.
It deals with the structure and functions of cells.

items.followUp: What are reproductive organs of a plant? Give two examples.

rubric.why: Credits explaining that vegetative organs are non-reproductive parts concerned with growth and nutrition.
rubric.description: Vegetative organs are the non-reproductive parts of a plant that perform functions such as growth and nutrition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an accurate definition.

rubric.why: Credits giving two correct examples of vegetative organs.
rubric.description: Roots, stems and leaves are examples of vegetative organs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct examples.

modelAnswer: Vegetative organs are the non-reproductive parts of a plant that perform functions such as growth and nutrition.
Roots, stems and leaves are vegetative organs.

items.followUp: What is a variable in an experiment? Give an example of one variable that should be kept constant.

rubric.why: Credits explaining that a control is a comparison setup without the factor being investigated.
rubric.description: A control is an experimental setup used for comparison, in which the factor being investigated is absent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of a control.

rubric.why: Credits a relevant example of a control setup.
rubric.description: A similar plant grown without fertilizer can serve as the control when testing fertilizer's effect on growth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an appropriate example.

modelAnswer: A control is an experimental setup used for comparison, in which the factor being investigated is absent.
For example, when testing the effect of fertilizer on plant growth, a similar plant grown without fertilizer is the control.

items.followUp: State two human activities that can lead to species extinction.

rubric.why: Credits habitat destruction or loss as a cause of extinction.
rubric.description: Destruction of natural habitats, such as deforestation, can cause species to become extinct.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid cause.

rubric.why: Credits a second valid cause of species extinction.
rubric.description: Overhunting or overexploitation, pollution, climate change and invasive species are other causes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct valid cause.

modelAnswer: Two major causes of species extinction are destruction of natural habitats and overhunting or overexploitation of organisms.
Pollution, climate change and the introduction of invasive species can also cause extinction.

items.followUp: How can climate and habitat conditions affect biodiversity in a region?

rubric.why: Credits two factors that affect the diversity of organisms in a region.
rubric.description: Climate and soil are factors on which regional diversity depends.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both climate and soil are identified.

rubric.why: Credits the other two textbook factors affecting regional diversity.
rubric.description: Latitude and altitude are also factors on which regional diversity depends.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both latitude and altitude are identified.

modelAnswer: The diversity of organisms in a region depends on its climate and soil.
It also depends on the latitude and altitude of the region.
